note: Edge segments measured on the repo image with sub-pixel edge fitting along hand-placed search segments (no pixels of the photograph are stored here). The photograph (区大伟) is framed by a white border; the picture area 1488 x 883 px is taken as uncropped and its centre as the principal point. World lines: the 1923 portal and the towers of Teaching Block 1 (data/buildings/yihao.json, porch.portal, parts.towers) and the rock plinth (data/site.json, taihu.plinth: north face y 31.6, top z 0.75, foot on the road at z 0). The plinth's north-west corner reads 7 deg off vertical on the photograph (chipped arris or edge halo) and has a low weight. A west-tower corner under the side-porch roof (edge fit rms 3.2 px) was tried and dropped: it disagreed by 15-17 px with every other feature, most likely because it is a side-porch pier, not the tower. With the plinth's length (7.5 m) and position taken from hero-2560 and the steps, its height comes out 0.78 m (model 0.75) and the portal 9.5 m wide over the piers (model 8.8 m). Letting the plinth's y float as well moves it 2-4 m south with a loosely determined value (y 27.3-29.4) and a barely better fit, so the steps/Esri position (north face y 31.6) is kept.
